obligation: FSMA Intentional Adulteration (food defense) rule: Meat Processing
basis: Part 121 covers facilities required to register under FD&C Act section 415 (21 CFR 121.1). Plant 6 is registered because its plant-based line makes FDA-regulated food, so the 1.226(g) exemption for facilities regulated exclusively by USDA does not apply. Not a very small business (121.5(a)), and with 45,000 employees not a small business (121.3). Plants 1 to 5 are regulated exclusively by FSIS and not registered, so Part 121 does not apply to them; the group applies the same method there voluntarily

obligation: FSMA Intentional Adulteration rule: Food Distribution
basis: The five DCs are registered but only hold food in packaged form and have no liquid storage tanks, so the holding exemption applies

obligation: FSMA Intentional Adulteration rule: Grocery Retail and group
basis: Stores are retail food establishments, which do not register; corporate shared services hold no food

obligation: CIRCIA (proposed 6 CFR Part 226): all divisions and group
basis: No final rule. As proposed (226.2(a)), the group exceeds the SBA size standard for each division's NAICS code and would be covered. Tracked

obligation: USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System: all divisions
basis: No division operates an MTSA-regulated facility or a U.S.-flagged vessel

obligation: FSIS HACCP systems, including computer records: Meat Processing
basis: Each plant is an FSIS official establishment under a federal grant of inspection; HACCP records kept on computers need integrity controls for electronic data and signatures (417.5(d))

obligation: FSIS recalls and 24-hour notice: Meat Processing
basis: Official establishments must notify the FSIS District Office within 24 hours of learning or determining that adulterated or misbranded product entered commerce, and keep written recall procedures

obligation: FSIS HACCP and recall rules: Food Distribution, Grocery Retail and group
basis: No DC, store or corporate site is an official establishment

obligation: FSIS records and registration (9 CFR 320.1, 320.5): Meat Processing
basis: Official establishments keep 320.1 records; 320.5(c) does not require them to register as wholesalers

obligation: FSIS registration and transaction records: Food Distribution
basis: The division is a meat wholesaler and public warehouseman registered with FSIS and keeps transaction records in the ERP and WMS

obligation: FSIS grinding records: Grocery Retail
basis: In-store meat counters grind beef, and grinding logs are kept on store scales

obligation: FDA food facility registration: Meat Processing
basis: Plant 6 is registered (plant-based line); Plants 1 to 5 are regulated exclusively by USDA and exempt (1.226(g)); renewal window 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31 (1.230(b))

obligation: FDA food facility registration: Food Distribution
basis: The DCs hold FDA-regulated food

obligation: FDA food facility registration: Grocery Retail
basis: Stores are retail food establishments whose primary function is selling food directly to consumers

obligation: Refrigerated storage of packaged food: Food Distribution
basis: Facilities solely storing unexposed packaged food that needs time and temperature control must monitor temperature, take corrective action, verify and keep records

obligation: FDA preventive controls: Meat Processing (Plant 6 plant-based line)
applies: Yes (Plant 6 FDA line); not scored in this sample
basis: Plant 6's FDA-regulated line is under Part 117 preventive controls; outside the scope of this analysis

obligation: Sanitary transportation of human food: Food Distribution
basis: The private fleet of about 900 refrigerated trailers carries food the division ships, loads and receives

obligation: Sanitary transportation: Meat Processing and Grocery Retail
applies: Plant 6 as shipper and stores as receivers; Plants 1 to 5 outside the subpart
basis: 1.900(b)(3) excludes food in facilities regulated exclusively by USDA; not scored in this sample

obligation: Food Traceability Rule: Food Distribution and Grocery Retail
citation: 21 CFR Part 1, Subpart S (1.1300 et seq.)
applies: Yes for listed foods; FDA will not enforce before 2028-07-20 (tracked)
basis: The DCs and stores handle foods on the Food Traceability List; Plant 6 products contain no listed foods today

obligation: Reportable Food Registry: Meat Processing (Plant 6) and Food Distribution
basis: A responsible party is a registered food facility; stores do not register

obligation: OSHA Process Safety Management and EPA Risk Management Program: Meat Processing and Food Distribution
applies: Yes (five plants, DC-1 and DC-3); context only, not scored
basis: Anhydrous ammonia above the 10,000 lb threshold quantity; managed by site PSM programs

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (contract): Grocery Retail
basis: The division accepts payment cards in stores and online as a merchant, and the acquirer requires an annual ROC by a QSA

obligation: PCI DSS: Meat Processing, Food Distribution and group
applies: No (no card acceptance); group common controls appear in the ROC responsibility matrix
basis: Neither division accepts payment cards

obligation: FACTA card receipt truncation: Grocery Retail
basis: Accepts credit and debit cards

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (also N44-45-R02): all divisions and group
basis: For-profit businesses in commerce. Analyzed for Grocery Retail (loyalty data use and the camera analytics pilot) and for AI vendor claims; Food Distribution 3PL security commitments and Meat Processing apply generally

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Grocery Retail
basis: The co-branded credit card is issued by a partner bank; the division extends no credit itself

obligation: FTC Red Flags Rule: Grocery Retail
basis: The division is not a creditor; the partner bank issues the co-branded card

obligation: CCPA/CPRA and CPPA regulations (also N44-45-R06): all divisions
basis: The group does not do business in California

obligation: COPPA Rule: Grocery Retail
basis: No child-directed online services

obligation: INFORM Consumers Act: Grocery Retail
basis: No online marketplace for third-party sellers

obligation: CMMC, DFARS 252.204-7012 and FAR 52.204-21 (N42-R02, N42-R03, N42-R04): all divisions
basis: No federal contracts or subcontracts in any division

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure: group
basis: The holding company is an SEC registrant; divisions contribute incident facts through the group and the disclosure committee

obligation: State breach notification laws: all divisions (Florida worked example)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171; each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Every division holds personal information of residents of the five states: employee and payroll data (all divisions), loyalty and online customer data (Grocery Retail) and driver location data (Food Distribution)

obligation: Acquirer and processor agreements: Grocery Retail
basis: Annual ROC by a QSA and card incident notice to the acquirer

obligation: 3PL service agreements: Food Distribution
basis: About 60 external brands rely on group inventory records and temperature history; incident notice terms differ by contract version; 14 brands asked for a SOC 2 report by the end of 2027

obligation: Independent grocer supply agreements: Food Distribution
basis: Supply agreements with about 2,800 independent grocers and food service customers include notice terms

obligation: SOC 2 reporting: Food Distribution 3PL service
citation: AICPA Trust Services Criteria; 3PL customer requests
applies: Yes (planned for the 3PL service); Meat Processing and Grocery Retail are not service organizations
basis: 3PL customers rely on group controls for their own food safety records; the other divisions sell products to customers who do not rely on group systems

obligation: Cold-chain vendor agreement (inbound notice): group
basis: Group security terms added in 2025; the vendor's stated security incident notice is 72 hours from confirmation
